REVISION_HISTORY.trigger: Independent audit AX of PR #138 at 100169b9 / tree 4a981c49: RESULT=FAIL, BLOCKING=4, AUDIT_UNKNOWN=0. R2 does not defend R1. All four blockers plus the explicitly identified non-blocking defects are corrected here.

blockers_corrected.B-1: RESEND CONCURRENCY. R1 treated transaction atomicity as sufficient concurrency control and carried zero serialization vocabulary. Worse, no race is needed to break it: R1's own HPO-ASY-03 puts send and classification AFTER commit while HPO-ASY-05(iii) cancels the prior delivery INSIDE the transaction, so a resend issued while the first send is still in flight lets the first send's post-commit classifier write 'accepted' onto a row another transaction already cancelled. R2 freezes a SERIALIZATION INVARIANT (HPO-ASY-11) and makes CANCELLED TERMINAL with an eligibility-conditioned classifier (HPO-ASY-12).
blockers_corrected.B-2: DELIVERY / REQUEST IDENTITY. R1 declared a server-issued per-call primary key to be 'the ONLY idempotency key'. A per-call key is by construction not an idempotency key against duplicate submission: two submits mint two keys and both send. R2 separates INVITATION_ID / ACTION_REQUEST_ID / DELIVERY_ATTEMPT_ID (HPO-ASY-02), requires a durable, transactionally enforced uniqueness boundary for action_request_id, and freezes the outstanding-invitation invariant (HPO-ASY-13).
blockers_corrected.B-3: AUDIT VOCABULARY. R1 allocated 'evidence_tombstone.erasure_retry_requested' into a namespace governed by another domain, and made a test control depend on it. Canonical HPO-C.9 authorizes retry BEHAVIOUR, not vocabulary. R2 removes the verb entirely, shows the existing verbs already carry the distinguishing state, and discharges the audit vocabulary contract for the async-domain verbs that remain (HPO-ASY-14).
blockers_corrected.B-4: ERASURE IDEMPOTENCE MISATTRIBUTION. R1 claimed the versionsToSweep filter supplied 'the per-version idempotence a retry needs'. Re-measured: false. R2 replaces the claim with the measured mechanism, reframes the terminal determination around residual work rather than per-attempt operation outcomes so a retry can converge, and replaces the vacuous N-ASY-8 control.

nonblocking_corrected.C-1: PROVIDER ERROR DEFAULT — unclassifiable/no-key provider outcomes must fail closed into a non-success state, never 'accepted' (HPO-ASY-04).
nonblocking_corrected.C-2: PLATFORM/TENANT ROLE INHERITANCE — canInviteUsers inherits tenant role-hierarchy semantics under which the TENANT role value 'super_admin' satisfies an organization_admin-level check. Recorded explicitly; not conflated with PLATFORM_PRINCIPAL; platform-admin boundary deferred (HPO-ASY-08).
nonblocking_corrected.C-5: MANIFEST EXIT-GATE CONSISTENCY — postgres_requirements is now schema-consistent with exit_gates, and path fields carry the schema's own explicit UNKNOWN rather than prose in a path slot.
nonblocking_corrected.C-6: CANONICAL HPO-C WORDING — R1 narrowed HPO-C.10 to demo only. Canonical clause is 'Demo/lead requests must be durably recorded.' Both halves preserved (HPO-ASY-10).

RAT_ASY_01.title: INVITATION INTENT IDEMPOTENCY

RAT_ASY_01.no_cooldown_restated: No implementation under this authority may substitute a time window, debounce interval, or rate-limit bucket for the action_request_id identity. Idempotency here is identity-based, not time-based. A time-based approximation would refuse legitimate distinct intents inside the window and admit duplicates outside it — both failures of the ratified property.

MEASURED_CORRECTIONS_R2.method: Each fact below was measured against the working tree at the R2 parent (100169b9 / tree 4a981c49) by reading the named file at the named lines. Line numbers are this lane's own count, not inherited from any other document.

measured_sequence.969: let partial = false — a SINGLE SCALAR for the whole sweep.
measured_sequence.970_974: if (evidence.type === 'file' && evidence.filePath) { ... supabase.storage.from('uellix-evidence').remove([evidence.filePath]); if (error) partial = true } — the storage removal is attempted UNCONDITIONALLY on every entry, including a retry, and any returned error latches `partial`.
measured_sequence.975_982: for (const v of versionsToSweep) { if (v.content === null) continue; try { await eraseEvidenceVersionContent(v.id) } catch { partial = true } } — the guard at :976 is a CONTENT check (`v.content === null`), not a STATE check.
measured_sequence.984: const finalErasureState = partial ? 'erasure_partial' : 'erasure_complete' — derived from whether THIS ATTEMPT's operations all succeeded, not from whether any work remains.
measured_sequence.987: await markEvidenceVersionsErasureState(versionsToSweep.map((v) => v.id), finalErasureState) — applied UNIFORMLY to every swept version (statement at :987; its STEP 3 comment at :986).

erasure_idempotence_mechanism.consequence_1_the_filter_protects_nothin: Because :987 writes one state to all swept versions, a partial attempt leaves ZERO versions at erasure_complete. The versionsToSweep filter at :954 (which excludes only erasure_complete) therefore excludes nothing on the retry, and R1's attribution of retry idempotence to it is withdrawn (W-R2-4). The real idempotence on the content path is :976.
erasure_idempotence_mechanism.consequence_2_non_convergence: Because :970-974 retries the storage removal unconditionally and latches `partial` on ANY error, a permanently absent storage object whose removal reports an error pins the item at erasure_partial forever, even when the requested end state — content gone — has in fact been achieved. This is the convergence defect HPO-ASY-09 must close.
erasure_idempotence_mechanism.existing_audit_state_is_already_sufficie: The two governed log calls at :1017-1026 and :1028-1036 already carry, in afterJson, `versionsRequested` and `erasureState` + `versionsSwept` respectively, against AUDIT_ACTIONS.EVIDENCE_TOMBSTONE_ERASURE_REQUESTED / _COMPLETED. A retry is therefore already distinguishable from a first attempt through existing vocabulary and existing payload fields — which is why the verb R1 proposed was unnecessary as well as unauthorized.

INVITATION_ID.what_it_is: The stable business relationship/request record: public.invitations.id (db/schema.ts:140). One per outstanding invitation relationship between an organization and a normalized email address.
INVITATION_ID.lifecycle: Created once. A resend does NOT create a new one — it rotates the credential ON this row (HPO-ASY-05). Its status vocabulary (pending/accepted/revoked/expired) is the INVITATION's lifecycle and is never merged with delivery status.

ACTION_REQUEST_ID.what_it_is: The idempotency identity of ONE USER INTENT, per RAT-ASY-01. Opaque, generated once by the application/UI for that intent.
ACTION_REQUEST_ID.same_intent_replay: Transport retry, network retry, double-click and repeated submission of the SAME intent all carry the SAME action_request_id, and must produce the effects of ONE intent: at most one invitation, at most one rotation, at most one delivery attempt, at most one provider call.
ACTION_REQUEST_ID.new_intent: A deliberately new resend is a NEW intent and carries a NEW action_request_id.
ACTION_REQUEST_ID.enforcement_requirement: MUST be durable and transactionally enforced. A UI-side guard, a client-side disabled button, an in-memory map, or any process-local structure is NOT sufficient and does not discharge this requirement.

DELIVERY_ATTEMPT_ID.what_it_is: The identity of a SINGLE provider-attempt row in email_deliveries.
DELIVERY_ATTEMPT_ID.relationship_to_pk: The delivery table's primary key MAY equal DELIVERY_ATTEMPT_ID.
DELIVERY_ATTEMPT_ID.explicit_prohibition: It MUST NOT be described, relied upon, or tested as sufficient idempotency identity for a user intent. R1 made exactly that error (W-R2-1). A per-call identifier answers 'which attempt row is this?' and can never answer 'is this the same intent I already served?'

IDENTITY_MODEL.collapsing_any_two_is_a_defect: The three answer three different questions — which relationship, which intent, which attempt. An implementation that uses one identifier for two of these roles reintroduces either the duplicate-submission defect (intent collapsed into attempt) or the rotation defect (relationship collapsed into intent).

HPO-ASY-01.title: SCOPE — one table, no queue platform, no generalization
HPO-ASY-01.disposition: email_deliveries is authorized as a single, purpose-built table for provider-backed notification sends. It is NOT a queue, NOT a job table, and carries NO kind/payload polymorphism that would let an unrelated future notification type be bolted on without its own ratified decision. stripe_webhook_events and operation_tickets are reconciled as PATTERN references only and are not modified, extended, or merged. Discharges canonical HPO-C.1 and HPO-C.2.

HPO-ASY-02.title: Delivery / request identity and idempotency
HPO-ASY-02.revision: REVISED AT R2 — B-2. R1's 'the PK is the ONLY idempotency key' is withdrawn (W-R2-1).
HPO-ASY-02.disposition: The three identities of IDENTITY_MODEL are distinct and must remain distinct in schema, in code and in tests. Idempotency of a user intent is carried by ACTION_REQUEST_ID and by nothing else.

enforceable_uniqueness_boundary.required_property: For a given invitation relationship, an action_request_id may take effect AT MOST ONCE. A replay of the same action_request_id must be recognized and must produce no second invitation, no second rotation, no second delivery attempt and no second provider call.
enforceable_uniqueness_boundary.durability_requirement: The property MUST be durable and transactionally enforced — the recognition of a replay and the effects it guards must be decided inside the same transaction that would perform those effects, so that two concurrent replays cannot both pass the check.
enforceable_uniqueness_boundary.mechanism_left_open: The implementer MAY discharge this as a database UNIQUE key, an invitation-scoped request table, a constraint on the delivery row, or another equivalent durable mechanism. This authority deliberately does not choose, and a successor lane must NOT be required to infer a choice that was never frozen.
explicitly_insufficient: a time-based debounce or cooldown (prohibited outright by RAT-ASY-01)
a check-then-act SELECT with no constraint behind it — the measured shape of the current duplicate guard at lib/invitations/service.ts:52-64

closed_field_list_minimum: reference_id (the invitation or demo/lead record this delivery is FOR)
action_request_id (the intent that produced this attempt)
status (CHECK, exactly the five ratified states)
attempts (integer; incremented only by manual attempts)
last_error_code (CHECK, closed vocabulary — never the provider's free-text message)
queued_at / accepted_at / failed_at / cancelled_at (nullable; at most one terminal timestamp set)

HPO-ASY-03.title: Transaction boundary
HPO-ASY-03.revision: REVISED AT R2 — B-1. R1's implication that this boundary was sufficient is withdrawn (W-R2-2).
HPO-ASY-03.disposition: The email_deliveries row is created in status='queued' inside the SAME database transaction that persists the referenced business row and its audit entry — discharging canonical HPO-C.3. The provider call happens STRICTLY AFTER that transaction commits, never inside it and never inside any transaction — discharging canonical HPO-C.4. The measured precedent for this split already exists at app/app/organization/members/actions.ts:36-42, where createInvitation returns an unsent closure that is invoked only after withOrganizationDatabaseContext returns.
HPO-ASY-03.atomicity_is_not_isolation: STATED EXPLICITLY BECAUSE R1'S OMISSION OF IT WAS A BLOCKER. Wrapping writes in one transaction makes them all-or-nothing; it does NOT order them against a concurrent transaction, and it does NOT protect a row from being transitioned by work that is still in flight from an earlier committed transaction. Everything this boundary does not provide is provided by HPO-ASY-11 and HPO-ASY-12, and no clause of this disposition may be read as supplying it.

HPO-ASY-04.title: Provider attempt semantics and result categories
HPO-ASY-04.revision: REVISED AT R2 — C-1 (fail-closed default) and B-1 (eligibility-conditioned transition).
HPO-ASY-04.disposition: Exactly ONE provider call is made per authorized attempt. The result is classified into exactly one of the five ratified states before control returns, and the transition is applied subject to HPO-ASY-12's eligibility condition.

result_categories.queued: The row exists; no provider call has been made yet. This is the creation state, written inside the transaction.
result_categories.accepted: The provider accepted the message for delivery. Terminal for this attempt. Discharges canonical HPO-C.7: it is NOT a claim of delivery, receipt, bounce-freedom, or the recipient having seen anything.
result_categories.failed_retryable: The attempt failed in a way a human-initiated retry could plausibly succeed at.
result_categories.failed_permanent: The attempt failed in a way no retry of the same message will fix.
result_categories.cancelled: The row was superseded before or without a terminal provider outcome — by a resend (HPO-ASY-05) or by revocation of the underlying invitation. TERMINAL (HPO-ASY-12).

fail_closed_default.rule: If the provider adapter has no configured key, returns an unclassifiable operational error, or presents a failure this authority's closed error vocabulary cannot map safely, the delivery MUST fail closed into a NON-SUCCESS state. Classifying any of these as 'accepted' is prohibited.
fail_closed_default.default_state: A configuration or provider condition that MAY succeed after correction is represented as failed_retryable, unless a measured permanent condition proves otherwise. An unconfigured provider key is the canonical example: correcting the configuration and retrying is exactly the path to success, so it is retryable, not permanent.
fail_closed_default.no_invented_discriminants: This authority does NOT enumerate Resend SDK error shapes and does not invent discriminants for them. The classification table is built at implementation time against the pinned SDK, and until it exists every unmapped outcome takes the fail-closed default above.
fail_closed_default.why_this_needed_saying: MEASURED: lib/email/resend-client.ts returns null for BOTH the unconfigured case (:24-27) and the provider-error case (:37-40). An implementer wiring status onto today's return type sees only null and has no shape to discriminate on — so the default must be stated, or the cheapest implementation is to treat a completed call as success.

HPO-ASY-04.accepted_never_means_delivered: No UI string, audit verb, column name, variable name or test description introduced under this authority may use 'delivered' (or a localized equivalent implying receipt) for the accepted state.

HPO-ASY-05.title: Resend / token-rotation semantics
HPO-ASY-05.revision: REVISED AT R2 — B-1 and B-2 (serialization, intent identity, exactly-once rotation).
HPO-ASY-05.disposition: A manual resend carrying a NEW action_request_id: (i) mints a new raw token, (ii) rewrites the SAME invitation row's token hash and expiry — the relationship identity (id, email, role) is unchanged, only the credential rotates, (iii) transitions any prior still-actionable delivery for that invitation to 'cancelled', and (iv) creates a NEW delivery row in 'queued' bound to the same invitation and to the new action_request_id. Steps (ii)-(iv) occur in ONE transaction, under the serialization invariant of HPO-ASY-11. The provider call for the new token happens after that transaction commits.
HPO-ASY-05.rotation_is_exactly_once_per_intent: One new resend intent rotates the token EXACTLY ONCE. A replay of that intent's action_request_id rotates NOTHING and calls the provider NOT AT ALL (RAT-ASY-01). An implementation that rotates on every request to the resend endpoint violates the ratification even if each rotation is individually atomic.
HPO-ASY-05.why_rotation_rather_than_re_emission: MEASURED: the raw token exists only in the request that mints it — lib/invitations/service.ts:66-67 generates it and persists only its SHA-256 at db/schema.ts:145. It cannot be reconstructed from what is stored. Rotation is therefore the only mechanism that can produce a working link a second time, which is why canonical HPO-C.5 forbids the alternative rather than merely declining to require it.
HPO-ASY-05.explicit_prohibition: No column in any table may store the raw token in a form recoverable by the application — no plaintext, no reversible encryption, no keyed derivation that permits re-emission. Hash-only remains the sole persisted form.

HPO-ASY-06.title: PII minimization
HPO-ASY-06.revision: UNCHANGED FROM R1 in substance; retention clause re-anchored to canonical HPO-C.11.
HPO-ASY-06.disposition: No payload column, ever: (a) no rendered email body — it is regenerable from the referenced row plus the existing templates, so a stored copy is a second, driftable copy of the same PII for no operational gain; (b) no raw provider response — only a closed-vocabulary error CODE; (c) the recipient address is NOT duplicated onto the delivery row, but reached through reference_id, so exactly one durable copy exists; (d) attempts is a count, not a log of raw errors.
HPO-ASY-06.retention: NOT DECIDED HERE. Canonical HPO-C.11 assigns retention of these records to HPO-F. This authority defines no TTL, no purge, and no column whose default implies a duration. Inventing a placeholder number would itself be the prohibited act.

HPO-ASY-07.title: UI-visible semantics
HPO-ASY-07.revision: REVISED AT R2 — evidence re-anchored (C-7); memory-note citation removed.
HPO-ASY-07.disposition: The members surface may render delivery status per invitation as a SEPARATE, clearly-labelled field, never merged into or overwritten by the invitation's own status — the two answer different questions. Required vocabulary: 'accepted' must render as 'sent'/'accepted by provider' or equivalent and MUST NOT imply receipt; 'failed_retryable' and 'failed_permanent' must both surface a resend affordance; 'cancelled' may be hidden from the default view but must remain queryable for support and audit.
HPO-ASY-07.measured_basis: app/app/organization/members/actions.ts redirects to a fixed ?success=invited on every non-throwing path (:55), so the current surface cannot distinguish a delivered invite from one whose send silently no-opped. That is the defect this disposition closes, measured in the route itself rather than cited from elsewhere.

HPO-ASY-08.title: Manual retry / resend authorization
HPO-ASY-08.revision: REVISED AT R2 — C-2 (tenant role inheritance recorded; platform boundary deferred).
HPO-ASY-08.disposition: A manual retry or resend is authorized under the SAME actor and tenancy boundary as the existing invite/revoke actions: the permission predicate is canInviteUsers(membership.role) (lib/auth/permissions.ts:48-50), and the acting organization's id MUST equal the referenced invitation's organizationId — mirroring the explicit cross-organization refusal already present at lib/invitations/service.ts:131.
HPO-ASY-08.tenant_role_inheritance_recorded: MEASURED AND STATED SO NO CONTROL ASSERTS A FALSEHOOD: canInviteUsers inherits tenant role-hierarchy semantics (hasRole, lib/auth/permissions.ts:24-26, numeric dominance over ROLE_HIERARCHY at lib/auth/roles.ts:38-41). The TENANT role value 'super_admin' scores 100 against organization_admin's 80 and therefore SATISFIES this permission. A negative control may assert that roles BELOW organization_admin are refused; it may NOT assert that 'only organization_admin' passes.
HPO-ASY-08.platform_admin_boundary_deferred: The tenant role value 'super_admin' is NOT a PLATFORM_PRINCIPAL and must not be conflated with one. This authority does not resolve, narrow, widen or interpret the platform-admin boundary; that boundary is deferred to HPO-D and its lane. R2 fails closed against it: NO clause here introduces, authorizes or relies upon any platform-admin bypass of the tenancy check.
HPO-ASY-08.cross_org_is_mandatory_and_unconditional: Cross-organization authorization is mandatory regardless of role. No role value, tenant or otherwise, may retry or resend a delivery belonging to another organization's invitation.

HPO-ASY-09.title: erasure_partial recovery semantics
HPO-ASY-09.revision: REVISED AT R2 — B-3 (foreign verb removed) and B-4 (mechanism corrected, convergence required).
HPO-ASY-09.disposition: Discharges canonical HPO-C.9 ('erasure_partial is retryable, not terminal') as BEHAVIOUR ONLY. The terminal guard that today refuses re-entry for both terminal outcomes (lib/pipeline/evidence.ts:948) is authorized to be narrowed so that erasure_partial admits a further governed sweep, while erasure_complete continues to refuse re-entry exactly as today.
frozen_requirements: erasure_complete REMAINS TERMINAL — re-entry stays refused.
erasure_partial MAY BE RE-ENTERED through the same governed entry point.
A retry MUST NOT resurrect content. Nothing on the retry path may write content back, restore a prior value, or re-populate a cleared field.

Already-null database content is SKIPPED. This is the actual idempotence mechanism at this tree (the content check measured at lib/pipeline/evidence.ts:976) and it must be preserved, not replaced by a state check — because after a partial attempt no version carries erasure_complete to check against (MEASURED_CORRECTIONS_R2.erasure_idempotence_mechanism).
Deletion of an already-absent storage object MUST be treated idempotently, or otherwise monotonically, so a retry can converge.
A permanently missing storage object MUST NOT pin the item at erasure_partial forever when the requested end state has already been achieved.

A retry remains tenant- and project-scoped by the EXISTING authorization chain (requireOrganizationAccess, the erase-permission predicate, and project-ownership verification already present at the head of the function). No retry path may bypass, weaken or shortcut that chain.

terminal_determination_must_follow_RESID.the_correction: At this tree the terminal state is derived from whether THIS ATTEMPT's operations all returned success (the scalar at :984, applied uniformly at :987). That is what makes a permanently-absent object latch erasure_partial forever. The frozen requirement is that the terminal determination be a function of WHAT REMAINS — is any governed content still present? — rather than of whether each operation in this pass reported success.
terminal_determination_must_follow_RESID.consequence: If nothing remains to erase, the end state is erasure_complete even though an individual removal call reported an error for an object that was already gone. If something does remain, the state stays erasure_partial and the item stays retryable. This is what makes convergence reachable in finitely many manual attempts.
terminal_determination_must_follow_RESID.no_vendor_strings: The 'already absent' condition MUST NOT be established by matching vendor-specific storage error text. This authority freezes no such string and forbids pinning one. Acceptable means include making the removal monotone (an absent object is a satisfied postcondition) or verifying absence after the attempt — the choice is an implementation decision measured against the pinned client, not frozen here.

NO_NEW_AUDIT_VERB.withdrawn: R1's 'evidence_tombstone.erasure_retry_requested' is WITHDRAWN IN FULL (W-R2-3). No implementation under this authority may introduce it, and no control may require it.
NO_NEW_AUDIT_VERB.why_unauthorized: Canonical HPO-C.9 authorizes retry behaviour; it allocates no vocabulary. The evidence_tombstone.* namespace is governed by another domain, and the canonical ratification artifact states of itself that it does not override executable authority. A behaviour clause is not an allocation licence.
NO_NEW_AUDIT_VERB.why_also_unnecessary: MEASURED: the existing calls at lib/pipeline/evidence.ts:1017-1026 and :1028-1036 already emit EVIDENCE_TOMBSTONE_ERASURE_REQUESTED and EVIDENCE_TOMBSTONE_ERASURE_COMPLETED carrying versionsRequested, versionsSwept and erasureState in afterJson. A retry is already distinguishable from a first attempt through existing vocabulary and existing payload state.
NO_NEW_AUDIT_VERB.auditability_requirement_that_remains: The retry MUST remain auditable through that existing vocabulary and its existing afterJson state. If a future audit-vocabulary authority separately authorizes a new verb, that is its decision to make — not this authority's, and not an implementer's.

HPO-ASY-10.title: Demo / lead durability
HPO-ASY-10.revision: REVISED AT R2 — C-6. R1's narrowing to demo-only is withdrawn (W-R2-5).
HPO-ASY-10.canonical_clause: HPO-C.10, quoted verbatim: 'Demo/lead requests must be durably recorded.' The dispatch's operative refinement is that the durable record precedes the notification attempt.
HPO-ASY-10.disposition: DURABILITY IS THE POLICY. A demo or lead request that has been validated and accepted (i.e. is not a honeypot hit and is not refused upstream) must be durably recorded BEFORE any notification send is attempted, so that a provider outage, an unconfigured provider, or a thrown send can never be the reason the business fact is lost. This is the reverse priority from the invitation flow, and deliberately so: here the request itself is the business fact, not a delivery ledger entry about it.
HPO-ASY-10.storage_object_is_an_implementation_choi: This authority does NOT force a demo_requests table, does NOT force reuse of marketing_leads, and does NOT force a shared intake object. The storage object is an implementation choice subject to the existing schema authority that governs those tables. What is frozen is the property (durable record before notification attempt), not the container.

measured_state_of_both_halves.demo: app/actions/marketing/demo-request.ts performs zero durable writes today (module header and body measured). The policy is unmet here.
measured_state_of_both_halves.lead: app/api/marketing/lead/route.ts refuses before writing (LEAD_CAPTURE_POLICY_AVAILABLE = false) and, per its own measured header, would be refused by RLS in any case because the marketing_leads policies are scoped to database roles the runtime is not a member of. The policy is unmet here too.
measured_state_of_both_halves.honest_consequence: NEITHER half is operationally discharged at this tree. R2 records that rather than claiming the lead side is already satisfied. The lead surface's repair belongs to its own capability lane (docs/ops/capabilities/CAP_04_PUBLIC_LEADS.md); this authority states the durability policy that reaches it and opens no write surface there.

HPO-ASY-10.honeypot_unchanged: A honeypot-tripped submission must continue to produce zero durable rows and zero provider calls (measured short-circuit at app/actions/marketing/demo-request.ts:58-61). Durability applies to accepted submissions, not to deliberately-rejected bot traffic.
HPO-ASY-10.rate_limiting_out_of_scope: The existing per-IP in-memory limiter is unchanged and out of scope. Nothing in the canonical clause asks for durable rate limiting, and generalizing it would be the scope creep HPO-ASY-01 forbids.

HPO-ASY-11.title: SERIALIZATION INVARIANT for token rotation
HPO-ASY-11.invariant: FOR ONE INVITATION, CONCURRENT RESEND INTENTS MUST SERIALIZE. Two resend intents for the same invitation may not interleave such that both rotate, both supersede, or one's supersession is lost.
what_a_resend_transaction_must_bind_toge: the CURRENT invitation version / token identity it observed
the action_request_id of the intent being served
the supersession/cancellation of the prior still-actionable delivery
HPO-ASY-11.binding_requirement: These five must be decided against a single, consistent observation of the invitation's state and committed together. A transaction that reads the current token, then writes a new one without having excluded a concurrent writer from doing the same, satisfies atomicity and violates this invariant.
HPO-ASY-11.mechanism_left_open: The implementation MAY use a row-level lock on the invitation row, a compare-and-swap against the current token/version identity, or an equivalent version guard — PROVIDED the externally observable invariant is identical. Both mechanism classes already exist in this repository (MEASURED_CORRECTIONS_R2.serialization_precedent_in_repo), so nothing new is being invented.
HPO-ASY-11.provider_call_stays_outside: The provider call remains AFTER COMMIT. No lock, no version guard and no serialization mechanism may be held across a provider network call — the boundary of HPO-ASY-03 is unchanged by this invariant and is not relaxed to accommodate it.

HPO-ASY-12.title: CANCELLED IS TERMINAL — late provider results
HPO-ASY-12.revision: NEW AT R2 — B-1, the defect that needs no race.
HPO-ASY-12.frozen_rule: CANCELLED IS TERMINAL. A late provider result for a delivery row that has since become cancelled MUST NOT transition that row to accepted, failed_retryable, failed_permanent, or any other non-cancelled state.
HPO-ASY-12.eligibility_conditioned_classification: The post-commit result classifier MUST condition its transition on the delivery STILL BEING ELIGIBLE for that result. The state write is a guarded transition — it applies only to a row still in the state the attempt was launched from — and an outcome of 'no row was eligible' is a NORMAL, EXPECTED result meaning the attempt was superseded. It is not an error, not a retry trigger, and must never be handled by re-attempting the write unguarded.
HPO-ASY-12.why_no_race_is_required: STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE R1 MISSED IT ON EXACTLY THIS POINT: HPO-ASY-03 places the send and its classification AFTER the transaction commits, while HPO-ASY-05(iii) cancels the prior delivery INSIDE a later transaction. A resend issued while the first send is still in flight is therefore an ORDINARY sequence, not a race — and without this rule the first send's classifier would write 'accepted' onto a row that was already cancelled, defeating the cancellation's entire stated purpose (a row left 'accepted' asserts that a now-invalidated link was successfully sent).
HPO-ASY-12.late_result_observability: A late result may be recorded ONLY through already-authorized bounded diagnostic/audit mechanisms. It cannot resurrect delivery state.
HPO-ASY-12.no_new_vocabulary_for_this: NO new audit verb, status value, or column may be allocated merely to observe that a late result arrived for a superseded delivery. The five-state vocabulary is closed and this observation does not extend it.

HPO-ASY-13.title: OUTSTANDING-INVITATION UNIQUENESS
HPO-ASY-13.invariant: For one organization and one NORMALIZED email address, Commercial V1 MUST NOT create two simultaneously live PENDING invitation relationships representing the same outstanding invitation.
HPO-ASY-13.normalization_is_part_of_the_key: The comparison dimension is the NORMALIZED address — the trim-and-lowercase form the current create path already computes at lib/invitations/service.ts:50 before both its duplicate check and its insert. A uniqueness boundary keyed on the raw address would be trivially defeated by case or whitespace variation and would not express this invariant.
HPO-ASY-13.durability_requirement: The property MUST be durable and transactionally enforced. MEASURED: today it is neither — the guard at lib/invitations/service.ts:52-64 is a SELECT-then-INSERT with no constraint behind it in ANY schema lineage (MEASURED_CORRECTIONS_R2.invitation_uniqueness_census_all_lineages), so two concurrent creates can both observe 'no pending invitation' and both insert.
HPO-ASY-13.mechanism_left_open: A database UNIQUE key over the live-pending subset, an invitation-scoped request table, or another equivalent durable mechanism all discharge this. The implementer is not required to infer a choice: this authority states the property and leaves the mechanism open. The codebase's own precedent for the shape — a partial unique index expressing 'at most one LIVE row per key' — already exists at db/schema.ts:112 and is cited as precedent, not prescription.
HPO-ASY-13.future_ddl_disposition: If discharging this requires DDL: LINEAGE_REDERIVATION_REQUIRED=YES, and NO ordinal is allocated here (see FUTURE_DDL).
HPO-ASY-13.relationship_to_action_request_id: This invariant and HPO-ASY-02's are DIFFERENT and both are required. Intent uniqueness (action_request_id) stops the SAME intent from taking effect twice. Relationship uniqueness (this clause) stops TWO DIFFERENT intents from creating two live pending invitations for the same person. Neither implies the other.

HPO-ASY-14.title: AUDIT VOCABULARY CONTRACT DISCHARGE for async-domain verbs
HPO-ASY-14.scope: Applies to async-domain verbs only — verbs whose object prefix names an object this authority governs (delivery records and demo/lead request records). It does NOT reach, extend, or reinterpret any other domain's namespace.

named_and_preserved.LOCK-AUDIT-ACTION-VOCABULARY: NAMED AND PRESERVED. Declared at docs/ops/portfolio/PORTFOLIO_PF2_EXECUTION_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json:554 and restated at docs/ops/portfolio/PORTFOLIO_COMMERCIAL_V1_AUTHORITY_AMENDMENT_v1.0.1.json:265-270. It holds the AUDIT_ACTIONS object literal in lib/audit/logger.ts. THIS DOCS-ONLY LANE NEITHER ACQUIRES NOR RESERVES IT. A successor implementation lane must observe its release condition before writing that literal.
named_and_preserved.action_shape_rule: The executable shape pin is AUDIT_ACTION_VALUE_PATTERN at lib/audit/__tests__/logger.test.ts:24, applied to every governed value at :43 and asserted negatively at :66. MEASURED AT THIS TREE it is /^[a-z_]+(\.[a-z_]+)+$/ — two OR MORE lowercase segments. R2 records this precisely rather than repeating the stale two-segment description carried by an older authority (MEASURED_CORRECTIONS_R2.audit_action_shape_pin_is_not_two_segment_at_this_tree). Any async-domain verb must satisfy the pin as it actually reads at the tip where it is introduced.
named_and_preserved.executable_contract: tests/audit-action-contract.test.ts is the executable contract governing AUDIT_ACTIONS. It is PROTECTED: no edit may loosen an assertion, remove a registered site, add a correspondence exception for an async-domain verb, or narrow the scan roots. Authorized edits are ADDITIVE registration and ADDITIVE scan coverage only.
named_and_preserved.correspondence_requirement: Every logAuditAction call site must carry an entityType whose name corresponds to the action's object prefix, as enforced at tests/audit-action-contract.test.ts:158-172 (prefix derived at :172 via value.split('.')[0]).

scan_root_extension_is_an_OBLIGATION_not.measured_gap: CORRESPONDENCE_SCAN_ROOTS at tests/audit-action-contract.test.ts:87-99 is exactly ['lib/pipeline', 'lib/projects/service.ts', 'lib/portfolios/service.ts', 'lib/admin']. It does NOT include lib/invitations/**, app/** or app/actions/marketing/**.
scan_root_extension_is_an_OBLIGATION_not.consequence: Every call site an async-domain implementation would add falls OUTSIDE the correspondence scan today. The mechanism fails OPEN: an implementer who omits the correspondence entirely would see a fully green suite.
scan_root_extension_is_an_OBLIGATION_not.obligation: Any future implementation introducing async-domain verbs MUST extend CORRESPONDENCE_SCAN_ROOTS to include the actual new call sites — including, as needed, lib/invitations/** and app/actions/marketing/** — so the correspondence is genuinely enforced rather than vacuously satisfied.

async_domain_verbs_that_remain.status: PROPOSED VOCABULARY, NOT ALLOCATED AND NOT CREATED BY THIS ARTIFACT. No executable verb is added here; lib/audit/logger.ts is not touched by this lane.
async_domain_verbs_that_remain.conditions_on_use: A successor lane may introduce these ONLY after LOCK-AUDIT-ACTION-VOCABULARY's release condition is satisfied, only with the scan-root extension above, only preserving the protected surfaces, and only if they satisfy the shape pin as measured at that lane's own tip.
async_domain_verbs_that_remain.demo_lead_verb_deliberately_not_fixed: No demo/lead audit verb is proposed. The demo/lead surfaces are unauthenticated and open no identity or database context (measured), so whether their durable record is accompanied by an audit entry at all is an implementation question this authority does not pre-empt.
async_domain_verbs_that_remain.no_foreign_namespace: NO verb in any other domain's namespace — evidence_tombstone.*, tenancy.*, stripe.*, portfolio.* or any other — is proposed, required, or made load-bearing by this authority or by its companion manifest.

transitions: queued -> accepted            [provider accepted; applied only if still eligible per HPO-ASY-12]
queued -> failed_retryable    [failure classified retryable, or unclassifiable/no-key fail-closed default per HPO-ASY-04]
queued -> failed_permanent    [failure classified permanent by a measured condition]
queued -> cancelled           [superseded by a new resend intent, or invitation revoked]
accepted -> cancelled         [superseded by a new resend intent, or invitation revoked — the link it sent is no longer valid]
failed_retryable -> queued    [MANUAL retry of the SAME attempt row; attempts incremented]

terminal_states.cancelled: TERMINAL AND ABSORBING. No transition out, including from a late provider result (HPO-ASY-12).
terminal_states.failed_permanent: Terminal for this attempt. A new intent creates a NEW attempt row; it never transitions this one.
terminal_states.accepted: Terminal for this attempt, except for supersession to cancelled.

DELIVERY_STATE_MACHINE.no_state_named_delivered: Deliberate. A delivered/bounced/opened state would require provider delivery-event webhooks, which this authority does not authorize (see OUT_OF_SCOPE).
DELIVERY_STATE_MACHINE.no_automatic_transition: No timer, cron, scheduler or background process may effect ANY transition in this machine. Every transition is caused by an authorized human-initiated attempt or by the post-commit classification of one such attempt. Discharges canonical HPO-C.8.

OUT_OF_SCOPE: A general async job/queue/outbox platform serving more than one notification kind.
Any scheduler, cron job, or background worker.
Provider delivery-event webhooks (bounce/open/click) and any 'delivered' state derived from them.
Hosted Resend configuration of any kind (API key provisioning, sending domain, DNS).
Unifying the Stripe webhook event ledger with the delivery ledger under one table, one function set, or one migration.
Repairing the public lead-capture capability's policy/definer gap — named as measured context, owned by its own capability lane.
Deciding or defaulting a PII retention duration (canonical HPO-C.11 assigns this to HPO-F).
Any change to the timing, meaning, or payload shape of the existing invitation audit verb.
Any change to operation_tickets, cited as pattern precedent only.
Resolving the platform-admin boundary (deferred to HPO-D and its lane).
Introducing any executable audit verb, in any namespace.

FUTURE_DDL.applies_to: Every DDL consequence of this authority without exception, including the delivery table, the action_request_id uniqueness boundary (HPO-ASY-02), the outstanding-invitation uniqueness boundary (HPO-ASY-13), and any demo/lead durability object (HPO-ASY-10).
FUTURE_DDL.reason: No migration is written by this artifact. Shapes are frozen for a successor lane to implement against; ordinals, filenames and apply-order are not. The successor lane MUST re-derive the live next-available ordinal and the current DDL-lock contention state immediately before authoring any migration file.
FUTURE_DDL.no_identifier_is_allocated_or_reserved: This artifact allocates and reserves NOTHING: not ordinal 0070, not W2-28, not ODS v1.0.31, not Controller42, and no other successor identifier. Where such identifiers appear in prior measurement context they appear as MEASUREMENTS of what other lanes hold, never as claims by this one.

This is recorded as a measurement only; it does not imply that 0070 is this authority's to take, and the successor lane must re-measure rather than rely on this line.
